## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`m0003_drop_legacy_email` drops `users.legacy_email` without first taking the backup that every destructive migration in this codebase takes. If a deploy is rolled back, that data cannot be recovered, so the backup must be added before merge.

## Changes
Adds migrations `m0003` and `m0004`, which drop `users.legacy_email` and `orders.coupon_code`, and adds one test that runs all four migrations in order.

## Critical
- migrations/m0003_drop_legacy_email.py:7 — correctness — Call backup_table before dropping legacy_email — On any database with populated `users.legacy_email` values, `upgrade` runs `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email` without first calling `backup_table`, so no `users_backup_3` table is created. `migrations/safety.py:3-5` says "each destructive migration first calls backup_table", and both `m0002` and `m0004` follow that rule. — After this migration runs, `restore_table(conn, "users", 3)` fails and the dropped email values are lost permanently. — Fix: Add `backup_table(conn, "users", VERSION)` before the `ALTER` as in `migrations/m0002_drop_nickname.py:7`, then extend `test_drop_retired_columns` to insert a `users` row and check `users_backup_3`.
